captures.description: THE AI INCIDENT DATABASE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a free, open-source project managed by the Responsible AI Collaborative that indexes real-world harms, near-harms, and failures caused by artificial intelligence systems'. Four points: the aviation and cybersecurity reporting model, a scope of harms (bias, privacy, misinformation, deepfakes, vehicles, safety-critical failures), growth with deepfake and scam entries multiplying, and the MIT AI Incident Tracker as a research extension that parses the database with taxonomies and LLM pipelines. Six cards: the database, the MIT tracker, Partnership on AI, the OECD catalogue entry, a Kaggle dataset, a TIME clip.

captures.q: what counts as an incident in the ai incident database
captures.description: THE AI INCIDENT DATABASE'S UNIT, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: the definition from the Editor's Guide verbatim ('an alleged harm or near-harm event to people, property, or the environment where an AI system is implicated'), the adaptive criteria, 'three core baseline thresholds' (specific event, AI implication, harm or near-harm), CSET's taxonomy for categories, and the three entry kinds (incident, issue, variant). Nine cards, five of them the database's own pages (the guide, 'Defining an AI Incident', the about page) or papers on it (AAAI, ACM).
